issues.legal_issue: A writ compelling the grant or renewal of a mining lease is unavailable when the purported lease term has expired and no formal lease was executed.
material_facts: The tender for mining rights was accepted and possession of the area was given, but no formal lease was executed.
The purported twenty-year lease term had expired by the time the court considered the appeal.
The appellant sought, among other relief, an order directing the State to grant a lease or recognize an option to renew.
issues.conclusion: The appellant could not obtain a writ for grant of the lease or exercise of an option to renew it.
issues.legal_principle: Because the purported lease term had expired and no proper lease had been executed, there was no subsisting lease or renewal option on which to base a writ for grant or renewal.

predicates.lease_or_renewal_writ_proceeding: The proceeding seeks a writ compelling the grant or renewal of a mining lease.
predicates.purported_lease_term_expired: The stated term of the purported lease had ended.
predicates.formal_lease_not_executed: The parties had not executed a formal lease.
predicates.lease_or_renewal_writ_unavailable: A writ compelling the grant or renewal of the lease is unavailable.

issues.definition: When a proceeding seeks a lease or its renewal and the purported term has ended without execution of a formal lease, the output is that the requested writ is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: A government granting mining rights under statutory rules cannot collect a premium that the rules do not authorize unless the required prior approval for a special lease condition has been obtained.
material_facts: The State accepted a premium from the appellant in connection with mining rights governed by the Mineral Concession Rules, 1949.
The rules specified royalty, dead rent and surface rent but did not authorize collection of a premium.
The rules allowed other special lease conditions subject to prior approval of the Central Government, but that approval had not been obtained for the premium.
The appellant had received compensation for the unexpired period, which the court credited against the refund due.
issues.conclusion: The premium was illegally collected, and the State was required to refund the amount due after deducting the compensation already received.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 5 of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1948, the State was bound by the Mineral Concession Rules, 1949, made under that provision. Rule 41 specified royalty, dead rent and surface rent and did not authorize a premium; any other special lease condition required prior Central Government approval under Rule 41(3). The State could not impose a term outside the rules or disregard their requirements.

rule.if: regulated_mining_rights_proceeding and mining_grant_governed_by_statutory_rules and government_collected_premium and rules_do_not_authorize_premium and special_condition_lacked_prior_approval and compensation_already_received

predicates.regulated_mining_rights_proceeding: The proceeding challenges a government's collection of a charge connected with a grant of mining rights.
predicates.mining_grant_governed_by_statutory_rules: The grant of mining rights was governed by statutory rules binding on the government.
predicates.government_collected_premium: The government received a premium in connection with the mining grant.
predicates.rules_do_not_authorize_premium: The governing rules did not provide for collection of a premium.
predicates.special_condition_lacked_prior_approval: The government had not obtained the required prior approval for imposing the premium as a special condition.
predicates.compensation_already_received: The recipient had already received compensation that the court credited against the refund.
predicates.government_must_refund_premium_after_cre: The government must refund the illegally collected premium after crediting compensation already received.

issues.definition: When a government collects an unauthorized premium for a regulated mining grant without required prior approval, the output is a refund of the premium credited by compensation already received.
